# API management

The commands `mt help` lists under API management. More in [The mt command line](../index.md).

In a terminal, type `mt` and then the command. In the interactive shell and the cloud shell, type the command on
its own. `mt help <command>` shows the same details in your terminal.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`api-login`](#api-login) | Sign in with an API key or an email address and password, and save the sign-in (checked with the API first) *(not in the cloud shell)* |
| [`api-url-get`](#api-url-get) | Show the API URL commands use (MAITENTO_BASE_URL overrides the saved one) |
| [`api-url-set`](#api-url-set) | Save the API URL commands use (MAITENTO_BASE_URL, when set, overrides it) *(not in the cloud shell)* |

## api-login

Sign in with an API key or an email address and password, and save the sign-in (checked with the API first).

```text
mt api-login <auth-type> <identifier> [credential] [options]
```

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<auth-type>` | text | yes |  | key (an API key) or user (an email address and password) |
| `<identifier>` | text | yes |  | For key: the API key as &lt;userId>:&lt;secret>, or the user id alone; for user: the email address |
| `<credential>` | text |  |  | The key's secret or the password; leave it out to type it unseen, or pipe it on standard input |

| Option | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--no-verify` | flag |  |  | Save without checking the sign-in with the API first |

```text
Forms:
  api-login key <userId>:<secret>     the API key as one value (what MAITENTO_API_KEY holds)
  api-login key <userId> [secret]     leave the secret out to type it unseen, or pipe it: echo "$SECRET" | mt api-login key <userId>
  api-login user <email> [password]   an email address and password; leave the password out to type it unseen
The user id is the id of the USER who owns the key, not the key's own id: api-key-create and the portal show it with the secret.
The sign-in is checked with the API (GET /users/self) before it is saved; one the API rejects is not saved.
Saved sign-ins: on Windows, encrypted with DPAPI for your account; on macOS/Linux, NOT encrypted, in ~/.maitento/settings.json,
which only your user can read (mode 600). Where that matters, prefer MAITENTO_API_KEY from your own secret store.

Environment (overrides the saved settings for this process only; never saved):
  MAITENTO_API_KEY     an API key, <userId>:<secret>, used instead of the saved login
  MAITENTO_BASE_URL    the API URL, instead of the one api-url-set saved
  MAITENTO_NAMESPACE   the default namespace, instead of the one ns-set saved
  MAITENTO_CONFIG_DIR  the folder settings.json is kept in (default ~/.maitento)
Precedence: a command's own --namespace, then these variables, then the saved settings. 'config-get' shows what is in effect.
```

**Not available in the cloud shell:** it is already signed in as you.

Doesn't need you to sign in.

## api-url-get

Show the API URL commands use (MAITENTO_BASE_URL overrides the saved one).

```text
mt api-url-get
```

Doesn't need you to sign in.

## api-url-set

Save the API URL commands use (MAITENTO_BASE_URL, when set, overrides it).

```text
mt api-url-set <url>
```

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<url>` | text | yes |  | The API's absolute URL, such as https://api.maitento.com |

**Not available in the cloud shell:** it always talks to this Maitento API.

Doesn't need you to sign in.
